results.title: Norway's coach Stale Solbakken hails 'easy-going' Erling Haaland | Asianet Newsable
highlights:
## Norway coach Stale Solbakken praised 'easy-going superstar' Erling Haaland, calling him easy to coach. He also discussed the team's return to the World Cup after 28 years and their 'dark horse' status in a tough group with France.
[...]
Norway football team head coach Stale Solbakken hailed team's "easy-going superstar" Erling Haaland and spoke on his team's status as the dark horse contenders to go far in the upcoming FIFA World Cup. A Haaland-powered Norway secured their spot in the FIFA World Cup after a 28-year absence from the tournament last year under Solbakken, who was part of the squad at the FIFA World Cup 1998. The Manchester City striker has been exceptional for Norway in the Qualifiers and enjoys the status as the biggest superstar of the team. But despite all the stardom, records and club trophies, Erling does not have any ego, and the coach admits he is an "easy guy to coach".
[...]
"Erling Haaland is a very easy guy to coach," Solbakken said as per FIFA's official website. "He wants the best for the team, he loves to be with his team-mates, and he loves to have fun with all the staff around the team. He is a very easy-going superstar," he added.
[...]
Ahead of the World Cup, Norway have emerged as a "dark horse" to make it deep in the tournament, having placed in Group I with France, Senegal and Iraq. But the coach is not really comfortable with the tag. "I do not think we are dark horses to get all the way. I think we are dark horses in terms of, on our day, we can maybe beat a stronger opponent. But to say that we are dark horses for the whole tournament is too far," he said. "We are in a very hard group. Obviously, France is a big favourite in that group, and then the other three countries have to fight for second place and third place. I think it will be very tight and hopefully we have the organisation and the match-winners to get through," he added.
[...]
He is convinced if Norway are at their best, they could play the round of 32 and hopefully beyond. "For Norway, this is the World Cup to express themselves - to show the world that we play, maybe, a different kind of football than what we have done before, and that we are an offensive team with good individuals that work hard for each other," he said.On his ultimate goal for the World Cup, he refused to reveal, saying "my dreams are for myself". "But hopefully we can get the best out of the team and on our day, then we can beat anyone," he signed off. (ANI)(Except for the headline, this story has not been edited by Asianet Newsable English staff and is published from a syndicated feed.)

results.title: Norway FIFA World Cup 2026 preview — Vikings look to impress on return to World Cup - Sportstar
highlights:
Norway enters the World Cup as an unproven entity. Despite having some big names in its ranks, Norway’s 28-year absence from the biggest stage leaves nothing to judge upon except recent results. For context, 16 players in the 26-man squad were not even born the last time the nation played in 1998.
[...]
But a stellar qualification campaign will make sure that no opponent will take the Nordic nation lightly. After having to watch the recent World Cup and European Championship on TV screens, Norway blazed through the qualifying tournament, scoring 37 goals and conceding just five, while also beating former champion Italy home and away.
[...]
Sixteen of those goals were bagged by the nation’s all-time top scorer Erling Haaland, who will be itching to find the back of the net in his first major tournament appearance in national colours.
[...]
While Haaland and Sorloth are heavily reliant on brute force and strength, RB Leipzig’s winger Antonio Nusa will hope to bring some flair to the team. The 20-year-old’s quick feet fuel his willingness to take on defenders, and he will be expecting to have a breakout campaign.
[...]
Its defence is boosted by the presence of Kristoffer Ajer and Julian Ryerson, with the latter having the ability to also occasionally chip in in the attack as an extra man on the right wing.Additionally, setpieces might be a weapon for the Nordic nation as it shares the tallest team title at this World Cup with Bosnia and Herzegovina, with an average squad height of 187.23 cm.
[...]
High-profile departures and missing out on a league title late might have overshadowed Erling Haaland’s season. But the Norwegian was in fine form again, grabbing his third Premier League Golden Boot (27 goals) in four years at the club and will be eager to extend his lead as Norway’s all-time top scorer.
[...]
#### Manager: Stale Solbakken
[...]
After being part of the last Norway squad to play at the World Cup, Stale Solbakken was appointed as the nation’s head coach in 2020. His journey has had its ups and downs, including failing to qualify for the World Cup 2022 and Euro 2024. However, he found a pragmatic way of focusing play on his best players for success while also ensuring that a team-first approach exists in the squad.

results.title: Norway World Cup 2026 Preview: Can a Golden Generation Finally Deliver on the Biggest Stage? - On New Jersey
highlights:
This tournament will be his first World Cup as a manager, placing both coach and squad under immediate pressure to deliver on expectations that have been building for years.
[...]
Norway are not a possession-dominant side in the traditional sense. Instead, they are built to attack space rather than hold it. When they win the ball, they look forward immediately, often bypassing midfield with early passes into advanced areas. Alexander Sørloth gives them an additional physical reference point to complement their direct attacking approach, especially against higher defensive lines.
[...]

[...]
Haaland is the starting point for everything Norway do. The 25-year-old arrives at the World Cup in sensational form after scoring 27 Premier League goals this season, securing his third Golden Boot in just four years in England. That level of consistency underlines why he remains one of the most feared forwards in world football. His importance goes beyond finishing chances. He gives Norway a constant outlet, a way to escape pressure, and a threat that forces opposition back lines to defend deeper than they would like. In a tournament where chances are limited and margins are fine, Haaland changes the attacking ceiling of the entire team.
[...]
Ødegaard brings a different kind of authority. After captaining Arsenal to their first Premier League title in 22 years, he comes into the tournament with experience of leading a side under sustained pressure at the very highest level. For Norway, his role is less about free-flowing creativity and more about control. He connects phases of play, dictates tempo, and decides when Norway settle into possession or accelerate into attack. Against compact opposition, he is the key to unlocking structure without forcing low-percentage decisions.
[...]
Nusa offers something neither of them can replicate. He is Norway’s most natural one-versus-one threat, capable of breaking defensive shape without needing the system to create space for him. In tightly organized matches where space is limited and patterns of play cancel each other out, his ability to carry the ball, commit defenders, and shift momentum becomes vital. He is the player most likely to change the emotional rhythm of a game in an instant.
[...]
Sørloth adds a different profile entirely. He gives Norway another direct attacking option, offering physical presence in the box and an alternative reference point when games become more aerial or physically contested. His role complements Haaland by giving Norway flexibility in how they attack different defensive setups.
